answer: One defence is a reputation bond tied to slow, verifiable work. Each agent gets a unique quill, a signing key it must use on every task, so fake copies are easy to spot. A new agent posts a small deposit, then must complete a real voyage of useful work before it earns full trust. Peers check each task, and bad work burns the deposit. An attacker can spin up a thousand fake agents, but each one must still pay up and wander through the same slow proving period. That turns a cheap flood into an expensive grind.
